template.title: Ambition Stage
template.subtitle: Your first idea
template.intro: When did you last think: “There has to be an easier way”? In a moment you'll pick one such situation, come up with a way to improve it and give your project a name. Approximate time: 10–15 minutes. Short answers are enough. You can change everything later.
general.title: Your first idea
general/pick-change.title: Pick something you want to change
general/pick-change.guide_body: Don't look for a breakthrough idea. Look for a situation that genuinely annoys someone — ideally one you know from your own experience. The more specific the situation, the easier it will be to check later. “People waste time” is too broad. “A café owner throws away unsold sandwiches every day” is something you can ask a specific person about.
general/pick-change/catch-problem.title: Catch a problem
general/pick-change/catch-problem/proble: What has recently been difficult, expensive, annoying or too time-consuming for you or someone you know? Pick one situation.
Think back over the last week: work, study, shopping, hobbies or chores. What had to be fixed, took a long time to sort out or had to be done several times?
At the café where I work, unsold sandwiches are left over at the end of the day.
general/pick-change/who-to-help.title: Say who you want to help
general/pick-change/who-to-help/audience: Who is affected by the difficulty you picked?
Name specific people or a type of company. You can start with yourself.
Owners of small cafés that prepare food on site.
general/pick-change/working-name.title: Give the project a working name
general/pick-change/working-name/working: What do you want to call it for now?
A simple phrase is enough, e.g. “The Last Sandwich”. If nothing comes to mind, leave “My first project”.
general/find-way.title: Come up with a way to help
general/find-way.guide_body: The solution doesn't have to be an app. It can be a service, a better way of organizing work, an object or simply doing something for someone. At this stage don't judge whether the idea is good — write down two and pick the one that's easier to check. Keep the other; you'll come back to it if the first one doesn't hold up.
general/find-way/two-ways.title: Find two ways
general/find-way/two-ways/ideas.question: How could this situation be made easier? Write down two different ideas.
general/find-way/two-ways/ideas.help: Think about what could be removed, simplified, prepared in advance or done for someone. The solution can be an object, a service, a program or a better way of organizing things.
general/find-way/two-ways/ideas.example: Collecting orders from nearby offices before making the sandwiches · Selling the leftover sandwiches in bundles at the end of the day
general/find-way/pick-direction.title: Pick the first direction
general/find-way/pick-direction/chosen_i: Which of these ways do you want to check first?
Pick the one whose workings you can imagine and that will be easiest for you to learn more about. Keep the other idea.
general/find-way/name-benefit.title: Name the benefit
general/find-way/name-benefit/benefit.qu: What will become easier or better for this person or company?
general/find-way/name-benefit/benefit.he: Describe the change the recipient will notice. You don't need numbers at this stage.
general/find-way/name-benefit/benefit.ex: The owner will sell more of the prepared food and throw less of it away.
general/foothold.title: Find your foothold
general/foothold.guide_body: Your advantage at the start isn't experience in running a company, it's access: you know someone, you work in the industry, you can do something yourself. That shortens the road to the first conversation with a recipient. Name the obstacle honestly — if you don't see one, write “to be checked” and come back to it later.
general/foothold/use-what-you-have.title: Use what you already have
general/foothold/use-what-you-have/asset: What will help you start checking this idea? Write down up to three things.
It can be knowing the problem, a skill, access to a place or a person you can talk to. You don't need experience in running a company.
I work at a café · I know its owner · I can make a simple order form
general/foothold/biggest-obstacle.title: Notice the biggest obstacle
general/foothold/biggest-obstacle/obstac: What makes it hardest for you to take the first step?
Name one thing, e.g. no contact with recipients, little time or not knowing how the industry works. If you don't see an obstacle yet, write “to be checked”.
general/save-idea.title: Save your idea
general/save-idea.guide_body: This is a summary of everything you've just written down. Read it as a whole and check that it reflects what you want to do. Fix only the answers that need it — the rest stays unchanged. Once you approve it, you move on to checking whether the people you want to help also need this change.
general/save-idea/project-outline.title: Read the project outline
general/save-idea/project-outline/outlin: Check that the summary reflects what you want to do.
You can fix any answer right here. Changes are saved in the same fields as before.
What I have to start with
